name: Teruaki Sato
figure_note: No. 8: his Hanshin number (2021–26). Cubs number not announced yet (27 Nov 2026).
status: Signed with the Chicago Cubs (USA). The club announced a 6-year contract on 27 Nov 2026 (28 Nov in Japan). The reported total is $120 million, about 19.1 billion yen; one reporter says $125 million; the club has not published the money. His first press conference is on 30 Nov at Wrigley Field, Chicago. An MLB lockout (owners shutting the league during a labour dispute) is expected from 2 Dec.
summary: Left-handed power hitter from Nishinomiya, the city where Hanshin's Koshien Stadium stands. Unknown in high school, a record-breaker at Kindai University, the first pick of four clubs in the 2020 draft. In six seasons with the Hanshin Tigers he went from a rookie with 173 strikeouts, to being sent down to the farm team twice, to league MVP in 2025 and the Triple Crown (best batting average, most home runs, most runs batted in) in 2026. He left through the posting system (the rule that lets a Japanese club release a player to MLB in exchange for a fee) and got the biggest contract ever reported for a Japanese position player.
tiles: home runs in 6 seasons in Japan (803 games)
REPORTED Cubs contract, 6 years (about 19.1 billion yen)
Central League MVP awards in a row (2025, 2026)

labels.seasons_heading: Season by season (regular season, Japan's top league)

Management office for ads and media

An Instagram account, @teruaki_sato_8, is linked from his Japanese Wikipedia page, and magazines credit photos to 'his Instagram'. I did not open it, so the handle is not confirmed here. No X account found

seasons_note: Source: BASEBALL KING player page for 2021 to 2025; Daily Sports (28 Nov 2026) for 2026 and the career totals. The six seasons add up exactly to the career totals Daily Sports gives (803 games, 163 home runs, 518 RBI). RBI = runs batted in: how many runs scored because of his hits. The 2026 strikeout number is my subtraction: MLB.com says 327 strikeouts over 2025 and 2026 together, minus 163 in 2025. Not yet checked against the official NPB site.

timeline.event: Born 13 March in Nishinomiya, Hyogo. His father Hironobu was a national-level judo champion and is now a university teacher.
Grows up watching Hanshin at Koshien Stadium and joins the fan club. On visits to his grandparents in Miyagi, his grandfather teaches him the basics of baseball at a tennis court.
Enters Nigawa Gakuin High School, not a baseball powerhouse, at 177 cm and 65 kg.

Second year of high school: starts weight training with equipment his father set up at home and goes to a gym 3 or 4 days a week. He calls this the turning point for his power. Decides to aim for professional baseball.
Last high-school summer ends in the first round of the Hyogo tournament. He never plays in the national Koshien tournament. 20 high-school home runs. Chooses university.
Kindai University. Bats fourth (the cleanup spot) from the autumn of his first year.
Picked for Japan's university national team.

18 Oct: hits his 14th league home run, a new Kansai Big6 university league record. 26 Oct: four clubs (Orix, Hanshin, SoftBank, Yomiuri) pick him first in the draft; Hanshin manager Akihiro Yano wins the lottery. 12 Nov: signs; uniform No. 8.
Rookie year: 24 home runs, but 173 strikeouts and a long hitless run. Sent to the farm team (second team) in September for the first time.
Plays all 143 games: 20 home runs, 84 RBI.

Benched on 24 June and sent to the farm team by manager Akinobu Okada. Comes back; 24 home runs, 92 RBI. Hanshin win the league and the Japan Series. In December he leaves the team's celebration trip early to train at Driveline Baseball in Seattle.

14 May: a dropped throw at third base loses a game; sent to the farm team the next day for about three weeks. 16 home runs and 23 errors, the most in Japan. In December he tells the club clearly, for the first time, that he wants to go to MLB. Signs with the agency VC Sports Group around this time.

Breakout under new manager Kyuji Fujikawa: 40 home runs, 102 RBI, both the most in the league. Central League MVP, first Best Nine and Golden Glove awards. Hanshin win the league. In December he trains for five days in the USA with Mookie Betts, working on defence.
30 Jan: the last player in all of Japanese baseball to sign his contract, after long talks about salary and posting. 450 million yen plus 50 million in bonuses, a club-record raise.
March: World Baseball Classic. 3-for-10, 2 RBI. Japan lose 5-8 to Venezuela in the quarter-final in Miami on 14 March; he hits a game-tying double in that game.

Plays all 143 games: .306, 39 home runs, 106 RBI. Triple Crown, the ninth player in Japanese history and the first Hanshin player since Randy Bass in 1986. Hanshin win the league again. MVP for the second year running.
18 Oct: Hanshin tell him they will allow posting; announced 19 Oct. 1 Nov: posted. 2 Nov: talks open with all 30 MLB clubs.
24 Nov (US time): agreement with the Chicago Cubs reported, 6 years and $120 million. 27 Nov: the Cubs announce it. 30 Nov: press conference at Wrigley Field. 1 Dec: MLB's labour agreement expires.

achievements.item: Triple Crown (batting average, home runs, RBI): 9th player in NPB history, first for Hanshin since Randy Bass (1986), first Japanese-born Hanshin player ever
Central League Most Valuable Player, two years in a row
Home run title and RBI title (40 and 102; then 39 and 106)
Japan Series champion with Hanshin (the club's first since 1985)
Central League champion with Hanshin, three times
Golden Glove at third base (2025 confirmed; 2026 reported by J SPORTS)
Best Nine at third base (2025 confirmed; 2026 not confirmed, sources differ)
First left-handed hitter in NPB history with 20 or more home runs in each of his first three seasons
Biggest contract reported for a Japanese position player moving to MLB, and the first over $100 million (previous high: $90 million, Masataka Yoshida)
Kansai Big6 university league career home run record: 14, passing Tomohiro Nioka's 13
The other side: 173 strikeouts as a rookie, and 23 errors in 2024, the most among all 12 Japanese clubs

leadership_intro: Short answer: he is not a loud leader. Reports describe a calm, poker-faced man who does not show his feelings, and for years Hanshin fans read that as a lack of fight. What the record shows is a self-driven worker who went to America on his own to fix his swing, took two years of public scolding from his manager without answering back, and came out the other side as the best hitter in Japan.

leadership.title: A quiet face that fans misread
leadership.simple: He does not shout or show regret on the field. After his 2024 demotion, fans complained that he looked as if he did not care. A former Hanshin player answered that he was never that type and should not fake it; he just had to produce.
evidence: Daily Sports column listing the fan complaints (chasing bad pitches, no visible regret, 'no fighting spirit') and former player Yoshihiro Nakata's reply. The columnist reads the anger as the other side of very high hopes.
https://www.daily.co.jp/opinion-d/2024/05/16/0017657521.shtml
Number Web: coaches called him more sensitive than he looks.
https://number.bunshun.jp/articles/-/866569

leadership.title: He absorbed a hard manager
leadership.simple: Manager Akinobu Okada (2023 to 2024) criticised him in the newspapers and sent him to the farm team more than other regulars. Okada later said this was about basics, not dislike, and that he rated the talent highly.
evidence: Okada denied acting on likes and dislikes and said he wanted Sato to master basic plays. His words: 'Sato truly has ability.'
https://number.bunshun.jp/articles/-/866569
Benched on 24 June 2023 and sent down over attitude and conduct; he said then that he would take the lesson to heart (reported second-hand a year later).
https://www.daily.co.jp/opinion-d/2024/05/16/0017657521.shtml
After the 14 May 2024 error Okada said that was the end of it; Sato went to the farm team for about three weeks.
https://www.daily.co.jp/tigers/2024/12/24/0018477441.shtml

leadership.title: He went looking for answers himself
leadership.simple: After winning the 2023 title he cut the team's celebration trip short and flew to Driveline Baseball in Seattle, a training lab that measures a swing with cameras and sensors. Two years later he trained with Dodgers star Mookie Betts on defence.
evidence: Five days at Driveline in Dec 2023. The analysis showed his body drifting forward and a contact point too close to his body; he said he wanted to match feel and data.
https://www.daily.co.jp/tigers/2024/01/15/0017227629.shtml
He studies video of Bryce Harper and Freddie Freeman, who also throw right and bat left.
https://www.daily.co.jp/tigers/2024/12/24/0018477441.shtml
Five days of joint training with Mookie Betts in the USA in Dec 2025, on defence (headline and summary only; article not opened).
https://www.daily.co.jp/tigers/2025/12/19/0019828890.shtml

leadership.title: Team first, even when asking to leave
leadership.simple: When he first told Hanshin he wanted MLB, he said winning the title with Hanshin came before that. When the club said yes two years later, his first public words were thanks.
evidence: Dec 2024: 'This year was the first time I told them properly.' He also called his own 2024 season disappointing.
https://www.daily.co.jp/tigers/2024/12/24/0018477441.shtml
Oct 2026: 'I am grateful to the club for respecting my wishes.' He said his days with his teammates were truly fun.
https://www.daily.co.jp/tigers/2026/10/20/0020946995.shtml
Jan 2026, while unsigned: he said it was not a fight with the club and that they were talking properly.
https://news.yahoo.co.jp/articles/e9d822e648df975d2ed40b173f562702b22408bf

leadership.title: He gives back to his home town
leadership.simple: He donates 100,000 yen to childhood cancer support for every home run, and runs baseball clinics for children in Nishinomiya.
evidence: 1.6 million yen donated after the 2024 season, 100,000 yen per home run (headline only; article not opened).
https://www.daily.co.jp/tigers/2024/12/25/0018480826.shtml
Baseball clinic at Koto Elementary School in Dec 2025 and talk of a 'Sato-Teru Cup' youth tournament in Nishinomiya (headline only).
https://www.daily.co.jp/tigers/2025/12/01/0019764704.shtml

leadership.title: Respected by a pitcher who faced him
leadership.simple: Shota Imanaga, the Japanese pitcher who played for the Cubs, backed his move and said his power cannot be taught.
evidence: 14 Nov 2026 in Yokohama: Imanaga said the ability to hit the ball far 'is not something anyone can teach' and that Sato raises a team's strength. Their record: Sato 5-for-23 with one home run.
https://www.daily.co.jp/mlb/2026/11/15/0021035731.shtml

honest_view: He strikes out a lot. 173 as a rookie, 163 in 2025, 327 over his last two seasons. MLB.com says he swung at 53% of pitches and chased 35.7% of pitches outside the strike zone, and called that 'playing with fire' against MLB pitching.
CBS Sports puts his contact rate at 66% against an MLB average of 77%. A projection quoted by MLB.com (FanGraphs) expects .247 with 31 home runs in 2027: good power, modest average.

His defence at third base was a real problem: 23 errors in 2024, the most in Japan. He won a Golden Glove a year later, but the Cubs plan to use him mainly in right field, where he has played 262 games.
He was streaky for four years. Home runs went 24, 20, 24, 16 before jumping to 40. Only two of his six seasons are superstar seasons.
The contract number is not official. $120 million comes from US reporters; another reporter says $125 million. The club announced the years, not the money.

The price was helped by timing: few power hitters on the market, and Munetaka Murakami's 35 home runs for the White Sox in 2026 made clubs trust Japanese sluggers more. That is Chunichi Sports' reading, and several fans said the same.
My observation: the page leans on Daily Sports, a paper that covers Hanshin every day and is friendly to the club. Where a claim rests on a headline that I could not open, it says so.

headlines.original: 無名の高校時代からドラ1位　近大・佐藤のルーツ
headlines.english: From an unknown high-schooler to No. 1 draft pick: the roots of Kindai's Sato
headlines.why: The best single article on where he comes from.

roots.title: A judo champion's son
roots.text: His father, Hironobu Sato, was born in Miyagi in 1967, went to Sendai Ikuei High School and Nippon Sport Science University, and won the Kodokan Cup in 1991 in the 86 kg class. He was vice-captain of the university judo club when Olympic champion Toshihiko Koga was captain. He now teaches at Kwansei Gakuin University.

roots.title: Weights at home
roots.text: The father set up a bench press and dumbbells in the house. He taught punctuality, keeping promises, handing in schoolwork on time, and thinking only about what you can control. The son started lifting in his second year of high school and says that is when his power came.

roots.title: A grandfather and a tennis court in Miyagi
roots.text: His grandfather Isao taught him the basics of baseball at a tennis court near the grandparents' home. Isao died around 2024, shortly after watching one of his games. His grandmother Michie, 87, wrote in Daily Sports that when he points to the sky after a home run she thinks he is greeting his grandfather.

roots.title: A Koshien kid
roots.text: Nishinomiya is the home of Koshien Stadium. He grew up in the stands, was a member of the Hanshin fan club and admired Tomoaki Kanemoto and Kyuji Fujikawa. Fujikawa later became his manager in his two best seasons.

roots.title: Unknown in high school
roots.text: Nigawa Gakuin is not a baseball power. He entered at 177 cm and 65 kg, and a Kobe Shimbun headline says he even thought about the soccer club. His team lost in the first round in his last summer. He chose university while keeping the dream of turning professional.

roots.title: Kindai University: the record
roots.text: He batted cleanup from his first autumn. On 18 Oct 2020 he hit his 14th league home run, a three-run shot in the 11th inning, to break Tomohiro Nioka's Kansai Big6 record, with scouts from seven clubs watching.

roots.title: Draft night: four clubs, one ticket
roots.text: Orix, Hanshin, SoftBank and Yomiuri all picked him first on 26 Oct 2020. Manager Akihiro Yano drew the winning ticket with his right hand and said he drew on intuition. Sato called Hanshin a familiar local club.

roots.title: Off the field
roots.text: He is a known fan of the idol group Momoiro Clover Z; in 2022 he publicly congratulated a member on her marriage and said he would keep supporting her (headline only). No marriage of his own has been reported.

personal.event: Drafted first by four clubs; Hanshin win the lottery.
Signs his first contract at an Osaka hotel; says he wants to buy something for his parents. Given No. 8.
His father speaks publicly about the death of his university friend, judo champion Toshihiko Koga, who had sent congratulations on the draft.
His grandfather Isao, his first baseball teacher, dies shortly after watching him play (date from his grandmother's 2026 article: 'about two years ago').
Starts donating 100,000 yen per home run to childhood cancer support (1.6 million yen for 2024; headline only).

controversies.intro: No scandal was found: no report of a crime, doping, gambling or a personal-life scandal in Japanese or English (searched 27 Nov 2026; this was a light check of a few searches, not an exhaustive one). What exists is criticism of his play and attitude, a long contract stand-off, and tabloid talk around his move.

items.title: Record strikeouts and a first demotion
items.what: As a rookie he struck out 151 times by 9 Sep, a club record for a Japanese player, and went 35 plate appearances without a hit. Manager Yano had kept playing him through 104 straight starts.
items.outcome: Sent to the farm team; finished with 24 home runs and 173 strikeouts.

items.title: Benched and sent down over attitude
items.what: Daily Sports wrote a year later that he was benched on 24 June 2023 and sent to the farm team for reasons of attitude and conduct.
items.outcome: He said he would take the lesson to heart, returned, drove in 92 runs and won the Japan Series.

items.title: Was the raise to 150 million yen too much?
items.what: His salary rose to an estimated 150 million yen after the title. Social media split between 'too much' and 'fair' (headline only).
items.outcome: No consequence. The next winter his pay was frozen.

items.title: The error, the demotion, and 'no fighting spirit'
items.what: On 14 May, with Hanshin leading 1-0 in the eighth, he dropped a throw at third base and the game was lost. He was sent down the next day. Fans attacked his expressionless manner. He ended the year with 23 errors, the most in Japan.
items.outcome: About three weeks on the farm team. He admitted his numbers were down, took a pay freeze, then won MVP in 2025.

items.title: The last unsigned player in Japan
items.what: He was the only player in all 12 clubs without a contract four days before spring camp, because he and his agent were pressing Hanshin on posting as well as salary. Sankei Sports described the two sides as running in parallel lines.
items.outcome: He said it was not a fight. Signed 30 Jan with a club-record raise; posting talks continued and were approved in October.

items.title: Tabloid talk of 'forcing through' a move
items.what: Tabloid Nikkan Gendai wrote that he might force a move and would not back down. Tabloid-grade: recorded here as what was said, not as fact. More such reports are collected on the Shawn Novak page.
items.outcome: Overtaken by events: the club approved the posting two months later and he thanked it.

items.title: Is he worth it?
items.what: US analysts flag the strikeouts; MLB Trade Rumors had predicted 5 years and $80 million, so the deal beat that by $40 million. A few Yahoo! Japan readers called the price too high.
items.outcome: Open question until he plays in 2027.

deep_dives.title: How the door to America opened (2024 to 2026)
deep_dives.intro: Short version: in Japan a player needs nine years of service before he can leave freely. Before that, only his club can let him go, through the posting system. Hanshin had said no to others. Sato asked in 2024 after a bad year, was told to prove it, won the MVP, pushed again with an American agent, won the Triple Crown, and then the club said yes. The whole chase took 23 days once the window opened, because everyone wanted it done before the MLB lockout.

cells: Trains at Driveline in Seattle. Daily Sports later links his MLB dream to watching Ichiro on TV as a boy.

At his contract meeting he tells Hanshin clearly for the first time that he wants MLB through posting. He says there is no target year and the title comes first. Earliest free agency would have been 2029. Hanshin's Satoshi Shimamura answers that posting is the club's right, and that such ambition helps a player improve. No approval is given.
Says he wants to keep the dream. It becomes known that he has signed with VC Sports Group, the agency of Mookie Betts and Tomoyuki Sugano.
Trains with Betts in the USA. Tabloids call it the Dodgers 'fencing him in'. That is gossip; he did not sign with the Dodgers.
Talks between his agent and the club begin behind the scenes, according to a Sankei column. In mid-December he is on the team's championship trip to Hawaii.
Stand-off. He is the last unsigned player in Japan. He signs on 30 Jan and says posting and salary were both discussed at length, through his agent, and that talks will go on.
Sports Hochi reports the club is leaning toward yes. Scouts from the Rangers and Phillies are at his game. A National League official says clubs will try to finish before the lockout deadline.
Hanshin tell him yes on the 18th and announce it on the 19th.
Posted on 1 Nov. From 2 Nov all 30 MLB clubs may talk to him for 45 days.
Agreement with the Cubs reported on the 24th; announced on the 27th.

parts.heading: Why Hanshin said yes (the club's own words, through Satoshi Shimamura, head of baseball operations)
rows: Reason 1, results: over six years he reached 'a certain level', with 40 home runs in 2025, the Triple Crown in 2026 and back-to-back league titles. Fan support for his move also counted.
https://www.daily.co.jp/tigers/2026/10/19/0020945650.shtml
Reason 2, the times: more Japanese players aim for MLB and moving clubs is less of a barrier than before.
https://www.daily.co.jp/tigers/2026/10/19/0020945650.shtml
A strong wish alone is not enough. He pointed to Shintaro Fujinami (2022) and Koyo Aoyagi (2024) as cases where the club made the final call, and called this decision heavy and difficult.
https://www.daily.co.jp/tigers/2026/10/19/0020945650.shtml
Daily Sports adds its own reading: approving early gave him time before the 1 Dec labour deadline. That is the paper's view, not a club statement.
https://www.daily.co.jp/tigers/2026/10/20/0020946995.shtml

parts.heading: Why the Cubs, and why the gateway was open
rows: A gap in the outfield: Seiya Suzuki and Ian Happ both became free agents, so the Cubs needed a corner outfielder with power. Alex Bregman already plays third base.
https://www.cbssports.com/mlb/news/cubs-teruaki-sato-free-agency-contract/
They had done the homework: more than 50 scouting looks over two years, according to The Athletic as quoted by MLB.com. He also played against the Cubs in Tokyo on 14 March 2025.
https://www.mlb.com/cubs/news/teruaki-sato-prior-cubs-connections-before-contract
A human link: his Hanshin manager Kyuji Fujikawa pitched for the Cubs from 2013 to 2015.
https://www.mlb.com/cubs/news/teruaki-sato-prior-cubs-connections-before-contract

Earlier Japanese players went first: Suzuki (2022) and Imanaga (2024) both joined the Cubs from Japan. Both are free agents now, so he may arrive with no Japanese teammate. Whether either returns is not known.

deep_dives.title: The agent and the people around him
deep_dives.intro: Short version: his agent is Shawn Novak of the small American agency VC Sports Group, who works from Hawaii and speaks Japanese. Sato hired the agency two years before he left, and the agent, not a Japanese office, pressed Hanshin for him. Nothing is published about what he pays.

cells: Named by Sankei Sports, Sports Hochi, Number Web and MLB Trade Rumors. Same agency as Mookie Betts and Tomoyuki Sugano. See the new VC Sports Group page on this site.
Shawn Novak (ショーン・ノバック)

Sponichi (Oct 2026) names him as Sato's agent, the same as Sugano's, based in Hawaii. MLB.com confirms he is a VC Sports Group agent. He has his own page on this site, including the rumours about his talks with Hanshin.
Sports Hochi says he signed with the agency when he formally stated his MLB wish after the 2024 season. It became public about a year later.
No source explains it. One possible link (my reading): Novak helped negotiate ex-Hanshin closer Robert Suarez's contract with the club in 2019, so he was known around Hanshin.
Who pays the agent, and how much
No report. In general an MLB agent is paid by the player as a percentage of the contract; the percentage here is not public.
Management office for ads and media
No Japanese management office or sponsor deal was found. A tabloid hints at an advertising agency close to other Japanese stars; not used.
Satoshi Shimamura, head of baseball operations
He announced and explained the approval. The owner's and president's roles are not reported.
Opened by an empty outfield spot, two years of scouting, and his record. No named Cubs scout or executive quote found yet.
Home weight room, discipline, 'control what you can control'.
Taught him the basics in Miyagi.
Drew the lottery ticket; played him through a record strikeout run as a rookie.
The hard teacher: public criticism and demotions, 'to master the basics'. Later praised his ability.
Sato's boyhood hero; batted him fourth in both MVP seasons. Fujikawa's own words about him were not found.
Praised his full swing and told him to invest in his body. Given name not confirmed.
Five days of defence training together, Dec 2025 (headline only).
Publicly explained and approved his new swing in 2024 and 2025 (headlines only).

parts.heading: What this shows (my analysis)
rows: The pattern is new for Hanshin. The player hired a US agency early, the agency negotiated with the Japanese club directly, and the yearly salary talk became the lever: he stayed unsigned until the club at least agreed to keep talking about posting.
He is not with the agency that represents most Japanese pitchers (Wasserman, now THE·TEAM). VC Sports Group's selling points for a hitter are Betts's record contract and its work for Sugano.

The agent did not open the Cubs door alone. The Cubs had an empty spot and two years of their own scouting. The agent's value was the timing: getting the posting approved in October and a deal finished in 23 days.

deep_dives.title: Rumours and unofficial reports (NOT facts)
deep_dives.intro: Tabloids and weekly magazines wrote a lot about his contract fight in early 2026. None of this is confirmed, most of it rests on unnamed sources, and several predictions turned out wrong. It is kept here, clearly apart from the facts, because it shows how the fight looked from outside at the time.

parts.heading: Claims, who made them, and how they held up

cells: He was ready to 'retire' rather than sign, and go to MLB as a free man, accepting a ban from Japanese baseball. A former player said he no longer cared about Japanese baseball and would play in Mexico or quit if MLB failed.
Weekly Jitsuwa web, 22 Jan 2026; unnamed Hanshin beat reporter, unnamed former player, unnamed desk editor. Read in full by the owner.
Did not happen. He signed on 30 Jan, played all 143 games, and in October said his Hanshin days were truly fun. The echo of Hideo Nomo's 1995 exit is why the story spread.
He asked for posting 'next offseason' and did not give an inch at the table; the club said it was too early.
Consistent with what better sources say: Sports Hochi reported that he told the club he wanted to go soon. The club approved in October 2026.

His agent asked Hanshin to promise in writing that he could be posted after 2026, and would not start salary talks without it. A club source said a written promise was impossible before seeing how the 2026 season went.
Sankei column by Tetsuya Uemura, 9 Jan 2026 (free part read by the owner). Weekly Jitsuwa repeats it.
The best-sourced rumour here, but it is the club side's account. Neither side confirmed it and no written promise was reported.
200 million of his 500 million yen was a one-off 'title reward', leaving the base for future talks unclear.
Unconfirmed, and it no longer matters: there were no further talks with Hanshin.
Skipping the early joint training on 29 Jan hurt his standing with teammates.
Weekly Jitsuwa, 9 Feb 2026, a Kansai reporter.
He had no contract until 30 Jan and arrived with the team on 31 Jan. No teammate has said this on the record.
A move after 2026 was '100% gone' because the agent's tactics backfired.
Unnamed former Hanshin player, magazine article of 1 Apr 2026.
Wrong. Posting was approved on 18 Oct 2026.
The Dodgers were 'fencing him in' through training with Mookie Betts.
Wrong. He signed with the Cubs.

parts.heading: What the rumours get right (my analysis)
rows: The direction was right even when the details were wrong: he wanted out after 2026, his side pushed hard, and the club resisted until his results made refusal difficult.
The tone was wrong. The weeklies wrote of a break with the club; the public record shows a long negotiation that ended with thanks on both sides.
More on the agent's side of this is on the Shawn Novak page.

contracts.event: First contract with Hanshin, described as the top terms for a drafted player.
One-year contract, 450 million yen plus bonuses: a 300 million raise, the biggest in club history (the old record was Tomoaki Kanemoto's 290 million in 2007).
Hanshin announce they will allow posting.
OFFICIAL: Cubs announce a 6-year contract. Money not published by the club. Yearly breakdown, signing bonus, opt-outs and no-trade clause: not reported.

Release fee to Hanshin: $19,875,000 (about 3.16 billion yen), ESTIMATE. The rule: 20% of the first $25 million ($5,000,000) + 17.5% of the next $25 million ($4,375,000) + 15% of everything above $50 million (15% of $70 million = $10,500,000). The Cubs pay this on top of the contract, so their total cost is about $139.9 million.
The fee would be $20,625,000 (my calculation with the same rule).

money.changes_intro: Two rules explain this table. In Japan a player signs a new one-year contract every winter, and the club raises or freezes his pay according to last season; he cannot move to another club for years, so he has little bargaining power. The posting system then lets his club release him to MLB early: all 30 MLB clubs can bid, which is the first time in his life that the open market sets his price. The Japanese club is paid a fee worked out from the contract.
